senses.definition: a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual
the weaker part of a sword's blade from the forte to the tip
a minor flaw or shortcoming in character or behavior.
examples: The students admired their teacher despite his foibles.

senses.definition: a pate made from goose liver (marinated in Cognac) and truffles
a piece of thin and flexible sheet metal
examples: the photographic film was wrapped in foil

senses.definition: anything that serves by contrast to call attention to another thing's good qualities
examples: pretty girls like plain friends as foils

senses.definition: a device consisting of a flat or curved piece (as a metal plate) so that its surface reacts to the water it is passing through
examples: the fins of a fish act as hydrofoils

senses.definition: picture consisting of a positive photograph or drawing on a transparent base; viewed with a projector
a light slender flexible sword tipped by a button

examples: In this picture, the figures are foiled against the background

senses.definition: hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of
examples: What ultimately frustrated every challenger was Ruth's amazing September surge
their foiled attempt to capture Calais
many frustrated poets end as pipe-smoking teachers

senses.definition: an act of hindering someone's plans or efforts

examples: He foisted his work on me

senses.definition: sell as genuine, sell with the intention to deceive
